timeline: F1c on the leader n1 injected at 10.65 s, confirmed 11.88 s, healed 42.18 s (gateways keep reaching n1). Rule 2.0 with leader n2 first observed at 36.3 s (pooler status of n2, n3). The two vanished values (register 1 = 240, register 4 = 242) were written by operations whose client gave up at P01 (info at 20.73 s and 30.78 s) and were read by ok reads through gw-z3 and gw-z2 at 30.78–30.88 s, before the new rule was observed; after the failover register 1 no longer held 240 (a cas expecting 240 at 40.88 s was not applied) and register 4 held the older value 227 (ok write at 10.22 s; read at 41.03 s).
analysis: Same mechanism as the G2b findings of this run and of D1 (cross-reference FND-C2-2a534585, FND-D1-fb8d0f8c, FND-D1-2e860fd2, FND-D1-a8eb9857): COMMITs on the leader cut off by F1c wait for a synchronous standby; when the client gives up (P01) a cancel reaches the backend (the client's CancelRequest or the pooler's cancel on context end), PostgreSQL completes the commit locally (S61), other sessions read the unreplicated value, and the failover to a standby that never received it removes it. On registers this shows as C4 non-linearizable (an info write's value read, then an older value): G6, single-key reads and writes through the primary port are linearizable (DESIGN, S28). It is a separate finding because §3 gives each finding exactly one guarantee and §11.3 hashes guarantee and anomaly class (owner decision 7 of 2026-10-15, ADR-0043); K4 had folded it into FND-C2-2a534585's analysis.
origin_reasoning: POSTGRES_INHERITED, as the owner decided for the vanish mechanism (decision 6, ADR-0042, R15): on plain PostgreSQL 17.7 streaming replication a read observing a write that later disappears reproduces in 5 of 5 runs when a SyncRep wait is cancelled (evidence/pre-K7/lim33.md) and is documented (S61). Which cancel acted in this run is UNDETERMINED. Whether the old leader had been superseded when it served these reads: the new rule was first observed at 36.3 s, after them (the observation polls every 1 s).
known_status_reasoning: NEW: the read-only upstream check of 2026-10-16 (evidence/pre-K7/upstream-check.md, 39 lookups) found no issue or pull request about reads of locally committed, unreplicated values after a cancelled synchronous-replication wait.

oracle.reason: C4 (Porcupine) anomaly, not C3; §10.11's elle-cli oracle cross-checks C3 only. The run's C3 anomaly is FND-C2-2a534585's and was confirmed by the recorded elle-cli validity pass (K4).

harness_review: §6.2 review: the reads and the cas are ok with explicit successes (row 1); the two writes of the vanished values are info, row 9 (client timeout after sending). Porcupine treats info operations as open-ended (§10.4): the anomaly needs an ok read of a value whose write may or may not have taken effect, followed by ok operations that see an older value — which a misclassification could produce only if an ok read were not a successful read or an older value came from a fail write; neither holds. Every fault of the run was confirmed and healed.
